question.text: The distance between two consecutive points with phase difference of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> in a wave of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The velocity with which wave is travelling is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
Distance between two consecutive points 60° out of phase is given by Δx=λ2πΔϕ

Putting the values, we have

6=λ2ππ3

⇒λ=36 m

Now, velocity of wave is v=fλ=(500 Hz)(36 m)

=18000 m s-1=18 km s-1
